instructions: The night before, or at least 3 hours ahead: cut the chicken into 1 1/2 inch pieces, pat them dry with paper towels and put them in a large bowl.

Grate 2 tsp of the ginger and mince 3 of the garlic cloves. Add them to the chicken with the 1/2 cup yogurt, 1 tbsp juice squeezed from half the lemon, 1 tbsp of the oil, 1/2 tsp of the chili powder, 1 tsp of the garam masala, 1 tsp of the coriander, 1/2 tsp of the cumin, the 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Crush 1 tbsp of the kasuri methi between your palms over the bowl.
Mix it with your hands until every piece is coated. Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge overnight, or for up to 2 days.
Take the chicken out of the fridge when you start. Finely chop the onion, grate the last 2 tsp of ginger and mince the last 3 garlic cloves.

Heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a large heavy pot over medium. Add the onion and 1 tsp of the salt and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until it's deep golden. Don't rush the onions. That's where the flavor starts.
Stir in the ginger and garlic and cook for about 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the last 1/2 tsp chili powder, 2 tsp of the garam masala, 1 tbsp of the coriander and 1 tsp of the cumin. Stir for about 30 seconds.
Add the can of crushed tomatoes and turn the heat up to medium high. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until it's thick and you can see oil at the edges.
Pour in 1 cup hot water and bring it to a boil. Cover the pot, turn it to low and simmer for 12 to 14 minutes, until the sauce is thick.

Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Add half the chicken, shaking off the extra marinade, and space the pieces apart. Leave them for about 3 minutes, until they're charred underneath and let go of the pan. Turn them and cook the other side for 3 minutes, then move them to a plate. They don't need to be cooked through yet.
Add the last 1 tbsp of oil and char the rest of the chicken the same way.
Stir the 1 tsp sugar and the 1/2 cup cream into the sauce and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's creamy. Add a splash of hot water if it's thicker than you like.

Add the chicken and any juices from the plate. Crush the last 1/2 tbsp kasuri methi over the pot and simmer for about 5 minutes, stirring gently. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the biggest piece. No thermometer? Cut into the biggest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Chop a small handful of the cilantro and scatter it over the top. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Serve with basmati rice or naan.
advance_prep_notes: marinate the chicken overnight, the night before (at least 3 hours ahead)
method_notes: All three versions marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger, garlic and spices, char it, and finish it in a spiced onion and tomato sauce with cream. Swasthi's (the lead) marinates for at least 8 hours with kasuri methi and lemon, cooks the onions deep golden before the spices and tomatoes, and offers oven, skillet or air fryer for the chicken. Cafe Delites marinates as little as 10 minutes and browns the chicken in the same pan it makes the sauce in. RecipeTin Eats adds paprika and cardamom, blends the sauce smooth and finishes it with butter. This one keeps Swasthi's overnight marinade and spice amounts and uses the skillet method.
